clue.text: Mary Jane left to spruce up clothes

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it, so 'spruce up' dresses 'left' in its own letters

parts.note: to spiff up is to smarten or tidy
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone called Mary Jane leaves to tidy up her wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Jane looks like a woman's name, but it is slang for marijuana, and 'clothes' is a verb, not the garments. L slips in after SP to make SPLIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Jane is old slang for marijuana, and a spliff is a cannabis cigarette, so the slang names its contents.

clue.text: Insane rave-up to involve northern arriviste

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it inside, so the jumbled 'rave-up' wraps 'northern'
something insane is disordered, so the letters of 'rave-up' lose their sane order

parts.note: the letters of the party word, to be rearranged
N is the standard abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A wild party drags in some newly rich social climber from up north.
explanation.walkthrough: A rave-up is a lively party; rearranged it gives PARVEU, and N for northern goes in before the final U.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words come from French and describe a social upstart, someone newly wealthy who lacks established standing.

clue.text: Upstanding character, anti-beer, having slipped?

parts.note: the letter I stands upright, a single vertical stroke

indicators.note: letters that have slipped have fallen out of place, so 'anti-beer' is scrambled

parts.note: eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A teetotal pillar of the community who has fallen off the wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: I plus an anagram of ANTI-BEER gives INEBRIATE, and a sober citizen who has slipped is exactly a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a habitual drunkard, which is what an upright abstainer becomes after relapsing into drink.

clue.text: Entrance for bringing in antique article?

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so 'for' takes in the old article

parts.note: the word used as it stands
ye is the olde-worlde form of 'the', the definite article

explanation.surface: A doorway wide enough to carry in some old piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like an object for an antiques dealer; it is the grammatical article, and YE is the mock-antique 'the' of 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A foyer is the entrance hall or lobby of a theatre, hotel or house, the space you enter first.

clue.text: Bugs British character — and the rest — American sent back

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the run after 'British' is read right to left

parts.note: an air is a manner or character, as in an air of mystery
etc, et cetera, means and the rest
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A British figure, along with everyone else, was bugged by an American deportee.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers only the three pieces after 'British', so its B stays at the front. 'Character' tempts as a single letter, but here it means a person's manner or bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs is informal for germs or microbes, and bacteria are the commonest such disease-causing organisms.

clue.text: Bishop Sheen in Montana perhaps seeing Crow

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the American spelling of lustre, a sheen; Montana is one US state standing for America

explanation.surface: A cleric named Sheen, out in Montana, spots a crow.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheen looks like a surname (Fulton Sheen was a famous American bishop), and Crow looks like the bird or the Native American people of Montana; it is the verb to boast.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast loudly, and to bluster is to talk in a loud, swaggering, self-important way.

clue.text: Tax case with Conservative going for suspension

indicators.note: whatever is going is leaving, so 'Conservative' departs from the word for 'case'

parts.note: a cess is a tax or levy
a legal case is an ACTION; take out C for Conservative

explanation.surface: A tax lawsuit involving a Tory ends with him suspended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' reads as a lawsuit in the surface and really is one: an action at law, which loses its C. CESS is an old word for a local tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A cessation is a halt or pause in activity, as a suspension of hostilities or payments is.

clue.text: More paintings by Emin initially put up

indicators.note: in a down answer, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: paintings collectively are art
by as in multiplication, three by four, written with the times sign

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of 'Emin' is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the artist's surname

explanation.surface: A gallery hangs further works by Tracey Emin, the British artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like authorship but is the multiplication sign X. Tracey Emin is a well-known British contemporary artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional or in excess, so it serves as a synonym for more in phrases like extra time.

clue.text: Finer arts bias essentially causing stagnation?

indicators.note: the essence of a thing is its core, so only the inner letters of each word are wanted

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters
the word without its first and last letters
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A prejudice in favour of highbrow art stalls creativity.
explanation.walkthrough: Three words each lose their outer letters, and the cores run together. The question mark admits that inertia is a slightly loose synonym here.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to stay still or do nothing, the same lack of movement and progress as stagnation.

clue.text: Dry egg mixed with suet for pig

indicators.note: things mixed are stirred together, like ingredients, so the letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: six letters to be rearranged
four more letters for the mix

explanation.surface: A recipe: stale egg stirred into suet to make pig feed.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen surface makes 'pig' look like the animal being fed; it is a person who eats too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a pig means they are a glutton, and greedy guts is a British childish insult for exactly that.

clue.text: Fox conserving energy having paws thus endowed?

indicators.note: to conserve something is to keep it safely inside, so the fox holds 'energy'

parts.note: tod is a dialect word for a fox
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An energy-saving fox, and a query about the kind of feet it has.
explanation.walkthrough: TOD is an old Scots and northern English word for a fox. The definition runs on from the fox: its paws come equipped with toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Toed means furnished with toes, and a fox's paws are fitted with digits, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Naughty child brings sin into prominence

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside, so 'sin' goes within 'prominence'

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, a prominence in the landscape
to err is to sin or go astray

explanation.surface: A badly behaved child makes wrongdoing notorious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brings' and 'into' are split by 'sin' but work as one instruction. A tor is a rocky hilltop, familiar from Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A little terror is an idiom for a mischievous, unruly youngster who causes constant trouble.

clue.text: Still revolutionary keeps a role for US right-wingers

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the turned word holds 'a role'
a revolution turns something round, so 'still' is turned back to front

parts.note: still and yet both mean even so, or up to now
the article as it stands
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: A radical still has a job to do for America's conservative right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' fits the surface nicely, since the Tea Party took its name from the Boston Tea Party of the American Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tea Party is a populist conservative movement within American politics, broadly aligned with the Republican right.

clue.text: Large horn from Bath area

parts.note: a bath is a tub
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A big brass instrument from the English city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Bath look like the city in Somerset; it is just a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: Horn is a general term for a brass instrument, and the tuba is the largest and lowest-pitched of them.

clue.text: Welshwoman about to be circled by daring moggy

indicators.note: something circled by another is ringed round, so 'daring' surrounds the woman and 'about'

parts.note: pert means bold or cheeky
Sian is a common Welsh girl's name
ca, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman is about to be surrounded by a bold cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to be' looks like 'on the point of'; 'about' is CA and 'to be' just joins. Moggy is British slang for a cat, usually an ordinary one.
explanation.definitionFit: A moggy is British slang for a domestic cat, and the long-haired Persian is one particular breed of it.

clue.text: Does it move 14 Across to hedge?

definitions.meaning: read literally: what body part carries the Persian cat along? A cat is a puss, and it walks on its paws
to hedge is to avoid committing oneself

explanation.surface: A question whether the Persian cat moves to go into a hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic riddle read literally, a cat's paw; the second is the everyday verb for cautious evasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To pussyfoot is to act warily and noncommittally, avoiding a straight answer, just as hedging does.

clue.text: Man mentioned belligerent and dark lover

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so 'man' is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a man is a chess piece, such as a knight
a hawk is someone who favours war

explanation.surface: A warlike man with a taste for shadowy romance.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess the pieces are called men, and the knight is one of them. 'Dark lover' reads like a brooding romantic hero; it means one who loves the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A nighthawk is a person who habitually stays up or is active late at night, a lover of darkness.

clue.text: Director shows great intellect capturing scene after evacuation

indicators.note: to capture is to take and hold, so 'great intellect' holds the emptied 'scene'

parts.note: the physicist whose name is a byword for genius

indicators.note: evacuating something empties it, so 'scene' loses all its middle letters

parts.note: the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A film director reveals his genius by shooting a scene of a mass evacuation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a film shoot, which suits the answer. 'Evacuation' reads as people fleeing; it means emptying the word 'scene'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Eisenstein was the Soviet film-maker behind Battleship Potemkin, a pioneer of montage cinema.

clue.text: James in Iowa recreated Japanese island

indicators.note: 'James' sits in the rebuilt state name
something recreated is made afresh, so the state's letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the four letters of the US state
Jim is short for James

explanation.surface: A man named James rebuilds a Japanese island in the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: Iowa is a US state in the Midwest; its capital letter hides that it is only fodder. The nickname sits inside the shuffled state rather than beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iwo Jima is a small volcanic island south of Tokyo, site of a famous 1945 battle.

clue.text: Rudeness almost upset consumer

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of 'rudeness' is dropped
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the shortened word is rearranged

parts.note: the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: A customer is upset by rude treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a complaint to a shop, so 'upset' reads as offended; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The end user is the final person who actually uses a product, as opposed to a retailer or intermediary buyer.

clue.text: Bush with sharp spines: son lost much blood?

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so 'son' drops out of the prickly bush

parts.note: gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub
S is the standard abbreviation for son, here removed

explanation.surface: A boy pricked by a thorny bush bled heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost much blood' reads as one phrase, but 'lost' belongs to the wordplay and 'much blood?' is the definition. Gorse is common heathland scrub in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore is blood that has been shed in quantity, especially the spilt blood of violence or horror films.

clue.text: Spider perhaps too short — snooker player one to save?

indicators.note: cut too short means trimmed at the end, so the snooker support loses its last letter

parts.note: in snooker a spider is a type of rest for the cue; REST without its final letter
one who plays with a cue

explanation.surface: A spider is too small; can the snooker player come to its rescue?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spider' looks like the creature; in snooker it is a raised cue rest, one example of a rest, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer is a person who saves someone from danger, so it is literally someone whose job is saving.

clue.text: Honcho regarded as not seeing straight

parts.note: a head honcho is the boss
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: The chief is thought to be failing to see things clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a boss with poor judgement. Boss-eyed is British informal for cross-eyed or squinting.
explanation.definitionFit: Boss-eyed means having a squint or crossed eyes, so the vision is literally skewed rather than straight.

clue.text: Observer's complaint about Liberal showing elegance

indicators.note: about means around, so the eye complaint goes round 'Liberal'

parts.note: a sufferer from an eye infection; an observer's organ is the eye
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: The Observer newspaper grumbles about a Liberal politician's polish.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make Observer look like the British Sunday newspaper; it is anyone who observes, and an observer's complaint is an eye ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Style means a distinctive, fashionable elegance of manner or appearance, as in dressing with style.

clue.text: Smartest copper brought to trial

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: The cleverest police officer brought a case to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'trial' paint a police-and-courtroom scene; copper is the metal. 'Brought to' just places one piece before the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean clever or shrewd, especially in American and Irish usage, so cutest matches smartest.

clue.text: Drink scrumpy occasionally with secretary

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of 'scrumpy' is used

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: Having a drop of rough cider now and then with the office secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrumpy is strong, rough farmhouse cider from the West of England, which makes 'Drink' look alcoholic. A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is colloquial British for a cup of tea, which is a hot drink in the ordinary sense.

clue.text: Roman historian left with climber

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
ivy is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: An ancient chronicler goes off with a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; crosswords use it for climbing plants, and ivy is the usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: Livy was a writer of ancient Rome who produced a vast history of the city from its founding.

clue.text: Explosion in House as GOP offers way food's pushed down

indicators.note: an explosion blasts things apart, so the letters that follow are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An outburst in the US House of Representatives as the Republicans offer a way to force a bill through.
explanation.walkthrough: GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the Republican Party, and House suggests Congress; both are just letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: The oesophagus is the muscular tube, the gullet, down which swallowed food travels from throat to stomach.

clue.text: Voracious woman in shock at emergency room

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it, a mane
the word as it stands
ER is the American abbreviation for an emergency room

explanation.surface: A greedy woman in a state of shock arrives at the hospital's emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' reads as trauma, which suits the emergency room; it is a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is an informal term for a woman who pursues and discards many male lovers, an appetite for men.

clue.text: An artist embodies attendant spirit in city

indicators.note: to embody something is to hold it within a body, so 'artist' takes in the spirit

parts.note: the word as it stands
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword artist
in ancient Egyptian belief the ka is a person's spiritual double

explanation.surface: A painter captures the guardian spirit dwelling in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: KA is an Egyptian term for the soul or spiritual double that accompanies a person, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey, so it is one example of the general category city.
